result:
The proposed answer of 1349 rests on an invalid construction, so I reject it.

**The construction fails.** Take the rainbow triangle with AB = X, AC = Y, BC = Z. Attach leaves to pairs of the central vertices, as the solution does.

- A leaf v attached to A and B is forced to have Av = Y and Bv = Z. Any other choice breaks the condition at A or B.
- A leaf w attached to A and C is forced to have Aw = X and Cw = Z, by the same kind of check.
- Now A has the edge Av colored Y and the edge Aw colored X. These are different colors, so the condition requires an edge vw. No such edge exists, so the condition fails.

Only one leaf type can be used at each central vertex. The claimed "six groups of 337" with an even split of the colors is therefore impossible. Using a single leaf type unbalances the colors.

**The lower bound is also unsupported.** The claim that any connected graph with at least two colors has at least 2n − 3 edges is stated with no proof. Even if it were true, reaching it with a perfect three-way split is exactly what the broken construction was supposed to show. The solution gives no valid argument that 1349 is attainable.

I did not derive the true minimum, but I vaguely recall it being larger than 1349 (possibly 1350). That recollection is unverified. The rejection rests on the failed construction alone.

VERDICT: REJECT
